text:
Lori Loughlin Makes Major Comeback Following Prison Scandal
The digital comeback arrived on Monday via a clip where Loughlin’s former “Full House” co-stars—John Stamos, Dave Coulier, Jodie Sweetin, Candace Cameron Bure, Scott Weinger, and Andrea Barber—individually recited the iconic line, “Wake up, San Francisco!” Loughlin then appeared to reference a scene from the series where her character returned from maternity leave, stating in the video, “Hi, I’m Rebecca Donaldson, and I’m welcoming myself back to the show.” The video also incorporated archival footage of the late Bob Saget as Danny Tanner.
This social media re-entry aligns with a broader professional rehabilitation arc for the actress. Vicary noted in a statement via USA Today that the timing felt appropriate for the brand’s core themes of hope, positivity, and connection.
Loughlin’s departure from the public sphere stemmed from the 2019 college admissions bribery scandal. Federal investigators accused Loughlin and her then-husband, Mossimo Giannulli, of paying $500,000 to secure the admission of their daughters, Olivia Jade and Isabella Rose, to the University of Southern California as athletic recruits. The couple pleaded guilty to wire and mail fraud in May 2020. Loughlin served a two-month federal prison sentence and was released in December 2020, as documented by NJ.com.
Since completing her sentence, Loughlin has pursued a slow return to the screen. In 2021, she reprised her Abigail Stanton character on “When Hope Calls,” a Hallmark spin-off. She also appeared as a fictionalized version of herself in a 2024 episode of “Curb Your Enthusiasm.” Personal shifts have accompanied her professional steps; Loughlin and Giannulli announced their separation in October 2025 after nearly three decades of marriage. Around the same time, co-star John Stamos spoke in her defense on the “Good Guys” podcast, placing blame on Giannulli and stating, “She didn’t deserve to be dragged through that.”
Loughlin is not alone in resuming her career following involvement in the admissions scheme. Felicity Huffman, who served an 11-day prison sentence for her part in the scandal, has also returned to television with roles in projects including “Criminal Minds: Evolution,” according to reporting by Syracuse.com.
